claims.text: The baseline material is a fine-grained FeNiCrCoCu thin coating on a conventional metal substrate.
Controlled pre-annealing will increase the coating grain size relative to the as-applied baseline.
Increasing average grain size reduces grain-boundary density or total grain-boundary area.
Reducing grain-boundary density suppresses grain-boundary sliding during high-temperature sliding.
Reducing grain-boundary density suppresses dynamic recrystallization during high-temperature sliding.
Fine-grained coatings tend to activate grain-boundary sliding at elevated temperatures.
Dynamic recrystallization can occur in high-entropy alloys during elevated-temperature deformation.
Grain-boundary sliding and dynamic recrystallization localize deformation and increase wear.
Suppressing boundary-mediated deformation shifts the coating response toward bulk dislocation glide.
A coarser-grained FeNiCrCoCu coating will have lower wear volume than the fine-grained baseline during high-temperature sliding.
A coarser-grained coating will exhibit more uniform microscopic deformation and fewer localized grain-boundary-sliding features.
The proposed grain-size mechanism should dominate during sliding above 400 °C, where grain-boundary sliding and dynamic recrystallization are thermally activated.
At lower temperatures, alternative deformation mechanisms may prevail and the grain-size effect on wear may be less pronounced.
The magnitude of wear reduction and deformation-mode change depends on the degree of grain growth.
High-temperature phase changes may compete with the proposed grain-size mechanism.
Oxidation may compete with the proposed grain-size mechanism at high temperature.
